texts.preamble: Jagdish Ice Factory & Anr vs Fssai & Anr on 6 December, 2023 Author: Subramonium Prasad Bench: Subramonium Prasad $~78 * IN THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI + W.P.(C) 15672/2023 JAGDISH ICE FACTORY & ANR Th ve FSSAI & ANR
texts.facts: The Status Report reveals that Dr. Manisha Narayan, an officer of This is a digitally signed order. The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above. The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 07/12/2023 at 04:29:09 Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had directed for the destruction of the items in the factory concerned. 3. On 05.12.2023, the Counsels appearing for the Police and the Union of India were requested to hold their hands and on their assurance, this Court did not pass any order restraining the Jagdish Ice Factory & Anr vs Fssai & Anr on 6 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71615247/ 1 Respondents from taking any coercive action. It seems that despite the assurance given by the Counsels, the Respondents have taken further coercive action which is a violation of the orders of this Court. Inspector Bhupender Kumar, who is present is Court is also directed to remain present at 2:30 PM today. 7. This Court, in the presence of the learned Counsels for Union of India and the Delhi Police had given an oral direction to the Respondents not to take any precipitate action against the Petitioner and an assurance was given This is a digitally signed order. 8. In gross violation of the directions of this Court, Respondent No.1 has destroyed the goods lying in the godown of the Petitioner. 9. When the matter came up for hearing in the first round, Inspector Bhupender Kumar made a statement that Dr. Manisha Narayan, an officer of FSSAI who had directed for the destruction of the items in the factory concerned, was informed about the matter and the directions passed by this Court. In the second round he states that he had only informed Dr. Manisha Narayan that the matter is being listed for today. The Officer ought to have awaited the Orders of this Court especially when the matter was adjourned only for a day. 10. Let an affidavit be filed by Inspector Bhupender Kumar as to what was the information passed by him to Dr. Manisha Narayan. 11. Let an affidavit be also filed by Dr. Manisha Narayan that she was not informed about the directions of the Court. The Petitioner herein, Jagdish Ice Factory, has approached this Court challenging the sealing of the premises by the Respondent No.1/Food Safety and Standard Authority of India (FSSAI). 2. Since the factory is sealed and frozen meat was kept in the factory, with the passage of time, the meat in the factory has started decaying because of which there is a lot of stench in the area, creating nuisance to the people in the neighbourhood. that the factory be desealed for the purposes of removal of the meat inside the The goods lying in Jagdish Ice Factory & Anr vs Fssai & Anr on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97060414/ 1 the ice factory shall be disposed of in accordance with Section 38(4) of the FSSAI Act. 5. Inspector Bhupinder Kumar, who is present in Court, shall afford all Police assistance for the purpose of de- sealing and removal of the goods. The FSSAI shall also depute such technical officers which would be required for de-sealing of the premises. 6. It is stated by learned Counsel for the Respondent/FSSAI that there are two trucks outside the factory also containing certain meat articles.
